pitfall_name: JS↔WASM copy for witness and proof buffers
what_happens: Passing a 20-100MB witness array from JS to WASM via module function argument copies the entire buffer; benchmark shows 30-50% of wall time in 'proving' is actually JS copying and GC, not field work
why: WASM linear memory is separate from JS heap. When you pass a Uint8Array as argument to WASM export, bindings (wasm-bindgen, Emscripten glue) copy into WASM memory. If you keep JS reference alive, you have two copies, doubling memory pressure. No zero-copy path unless you write directly into WASM memory via HEAPU8.set()
how_discovered: Memory snapshot shows 2x allocation, and timing breakdown shows time before first WASM instruction is large; often wastes a day because flame graph attributes copy to wasm instantiation
mitigation: Pre-allocate WASM memory, expose malloc, get pointer, write directly via HEAPU8.subarray(ptr, ptr+len).set(jsArray). Or use wasm-bindgen with `&` that borrows from WASM memory, not JS. Reuse buffers across runs.

pitfall_name: SharedArrayBuffer requires COOP/COEP and breaks deployment
what_happens: WASM threads (wasm-bindgen-rayon, proving parallel NTT) work locally but fail in production with 'SharedArrayBuffer is not defined' or worker fails to spawn
why: Chrome/Firefox/Safari require cross-origin isolation: COOP: same-origin + COEP: require-corp headers to enable SharedArrayBuffer. Without it, WASM memory cannot be shared between workers. Many CDNs, analytics scripts, and OAuth iframes don't send CORP headers, so enabling COOP/COEP breaks third-party embeds.
how_discovered: Works on localhost (where browsers relaxed) but fails on staging; console error only in production; typically wastes 1-2 days debugging deployment headers, not code
mitigation: Serve proving page from isolated origin/subdomain with strict COOP/COEP, load third-party via COEP-credentialless or via proxy. Detect at runtime: if typeof SharedArrayBuffer==='undefined' fallback to single-threaded WASM build. Document requirement for deploy.

pitfall_name: WASM memory growth invalidates JS TypedArray views
what_happens: After some proving runs, output proof is corrupted or all zeros, but only intermittently after memory.grow
why: JS Uint8Array views are backed by ArrayBuffer that gets detached and replaced on WASM memory.grow(). If you cached HEAPU8 = new Uint8Array(memory.buffer) once at init, after grow it points to old detached buffer (length 0). Subsequent writes go nowhere, reads return zeros.
how_discovered: Bug appears only when witness size exceeds initial memory and triggers grow; symptom is silent correctness failure, not crash; often takes days because reproduction depends on input size crossing threshold
mitigation: Always re-create views after any call that may grow: memory.buffer !== heap.buffer check, or wrap in function getHeap() { return new Uint8Array(memory.buffer); }. In Emscripten use HEAPU8 = new Uint8Array(Module.HEAPU8.buffer) after grow.

pitfall_name: 32-bit 4GB address space ceiling for large circuits
what_happens: Prover OOMs at ~3.2-3.6GB WASM heap even on 32GB desktop machine; Chrome tab crashes with 'out of memory'
why: WASM32 is limited to 4GB linear memory (2^32), and browser implementations reserve some, with max ~4GB - 1 page. Many proving systems (Groth16, Plonk with large SRS, Halo2 K=20+) need >4GB for MSM/NTT tables. No memory64 in browsers yet as of 2024-2025.
how_discovered: Fails only on larger circuits; small benchmarks pass; error is WASM trap or tab kill without stack; mobile kills earlier at ~1-1.5GB; wastes week thinking it's leak
mitigation: Stream SRS, use chunked MSM, use WebGPU for large tables, or split proving into smaller segments. Track memory usage and fail early with clear error. Watch for memory64 proposal - not production in Chrome/Firefox/Safari as of 2026 Q1.

pitfall_name: WebGPU buffer mapAsync readback stall counted as GPU time
what_happens: Benchmark reports GPU NTT at 800ms but end-to-end is 2500ms; profiling shows 60% time in mapAsync + getMappedRange
why: WebGPU readback requires explicit copy GPU buffer -> staging buffer -> mapAsync which synchronizes CPU/GPU and stalls pipeline. If you time from dispatch to mapAsync resolution, you include queue flush + GPU->CPU copy + synchronization, not just compute. Also mapping without proper usage flags causes extra copy.
how_discovered: GPU timestamp queries show compute 800ms but JS performance.now() around whole operation shows 2.5x; developers attribute to 'GPU slow' when it's readback; wastes days optimizing shaders
mitigation: Use timestamp queries to isolate compute vs copy, double-buffer staging, use async pipeline with multiple buffers, avoid readback on hot loop - keep data on GPU for MSM if possible. Measure copy and map separately.

pitfall_name: Browser timer clamping and COOP timer resolution
what_happens: Repeated runs of same proof show 0ms or 5ms quantized timings, or variance 100x larger than real, making micro-benchmarks lie
why: After Spectre, browsers clamp performance.now() resolution to 5us-100us unless cross-origin isolated, and to 1ms in some contexts. Date.now() clamped to 1ms. In non-isolated context, resolution is coarse. Also event loop jitter adds 2-8ms variance. Measuring a 2ms field op with 1ms clock is noise.
how_discovered: Histogram of timings shows spikes at 0,1,5ms boundaries; same WASM function shows bimodal distribution; often misattributed to JIT until clock resolution checked
mitigation: Require cross-origin isolated context for high-res timers (5us). For micro-benchmarks, loop operation 100-1000x and divide, or use WebGPU timestamp queries (if available) which have ns resolution. Warm up and use median of many runs.

pitfall_name: JIT warmup and tiering distorts first-run proving time
what_happens: First proof in session takes 4-8x longer than subsequent proofs; reported 'proving time' depends on whether page was just loaded
why: V8/SpiderMonkey/JavaScriptCore start WASM in Liftoff (baseline) then tier up to TurboFan after hot calls. WASM->JS trampolines also optimized lazily. First run includes compilation + tier-up + GC. Chrome also compiles WASM modules asynchronously on worker threads.
how_discovered: Benchmark run in loop shows decreasing times over first 3-5 iterations, then plateau; first-run number is published as performance but not reproducible; wastes days comparing two implementations where one was measured cold
mitigation: Warm up with dummy circuit of similar size 2-3 times before measuring. Await WebAssembly.compile + instantiate fully. Report cold vs hot separately. Use performance.measureUserAgentSpecific? No, use explicit warmup and report median of runs 4-10.

pitfall_name: WASM SIMD128 not auto-vectorizing field arithmetic
what_happens: Compiling Rust/C++ with -C target-feature=+simd128 shows no speedup for Goldilocks/BN254 field mul, sometimes slower
why: WASM SIMD is 128-bit integer/float lanes, but field arithmetic needs 64x64->128 mul with carry chain (e.g., Montgomery). LLVM auto-vectorizer cannot map carry-dependent 64-bit mul to i32x4 or i64x2 SIMD. Hand-written SIMD using wasm_simd intrinsics required, and even then needs careful carry handling. Many crates compile but emit scalar fallback.
how_discovered: Inspect WASM disassembly: no v128 ops in hot loop, or only shuffles; benchmark shows same instruction count; discovered after weeks optimizing Rust expecting SIMD
mitigation: Write explicit SIMD kernels with wasm_simd intrinsics for NTT butterflies that are SIMD-friendly (addition/sub, not mul with carry), use lookup tables for mul. Verify with wasm-objdump that v128 instructions appear. For field mul, keep scalar Montgomery and use SIMD for NTT permutation.

pitfall_name: Cross-origin iframe cannot get isolation or WebGPU
what_happens: Proving widget embedded in dapp via iframe fails to create WebGPU device or SharedArrayBuffer even though top-level page has COOP/COEP
why: Cross-origin iframe inherits cross-origin isolation only if both iframe and parent set COOP/COEP and iframe has allow='cross-origin-isolated' attribute. By default, embedded context is not isolated. WebGPU also requires secure context and may be blocked by Permissions-Policy. Safari further restricts WebGPU in iframes.
how_discovered: Works when opened directly but fails when embedded in partner site; error 'WebGPU not supported' or 'SharedArrayBuffer not defined' only in iframe context; wastes integration week
mitigation: Require embedders to set <iframe allow="cross-origin-isolated; gpu"> and serve iframe origin with COOP/COEP. Detect at startup: check crossOriginIsolated and navigator.gpu. Provide fallback: if in iframe, redirect to top-level or use popup window for proving.

pitfall_name: Safari divergences: no timestamp query and late WASM threads
what_happens: Benchmarks on Safari show GPU time 0 or device lost, or WASM threads fallback to single thread despite code working in Chrome
why: Safari WebGPU implementation as of 2024-2025 did not expose timestamp-query feature to web content by default, and WASM threads (SharedArrayBuffer) shipped later and requires extra flags in some versions. Safari also has stricter memory limits (~2GB WASM) and kills canvas/WebGPU after background tab.
how_discovered: Works in Chrome/Firefox but fails in Safari with feature-not-supported error; often discovered only after launch by users on iOS/macOS; wastes time because Safari remote debugging is harder
mitigation: Feature-detect: adapter.features.has('timestamp-query') and typeof SharedArrayBuffer; provide CPU timing fallback when timestamp not available, and single-threaded WASM bundle for Safari. Test explicitly on Safari Technology Preview and iOS.
